rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'art' (McCloud)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scott defines art as "any human activity which doesn't grow out of either of our species' two basic instincts: survival and reproduction!"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: McCloud uses this deliberately broad definition to include comics within the domain of 'art' and to answer critics who ask, "Can comics be art?" The guide presents the quote verbatim and frames it as the foundational criterion for treating comics as art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comics qualify as art by sharing common characteristics of art
rubrics_metrics.description: Although comics differ from other forms of communication, Scott argues that all art shares certain characteristics in common and that comics fit within those characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the broad definition above to assess comics: despite medium-specific differences (covered in earlier chapters), test whether a comics work exhibits the common characteristics McCloud identifies for art. The summary emphasizes that Chapter 7 argues for commonality across art forms as justification for considering comics art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art's evolutionary purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Scott explains that the pursuit of art serves three evolutionary purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter illustrates these purposes with narrative examples (e.g., a series of panels showing a day in the life of early man). When evaluating or discussing a work, consider which of these evolutionary purposes the work exemplifies — the guide notes the tripartite purpose but does not enumerate the three in this excerpt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sequential panels as illustrative technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a series of panels to display a day in the life of early Man, Scott demonstrates distinctions between instinct-driven behavior and the pursuit of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study guide highlights this technique as both an explanatory device in McCloud's argument and a core comics method: sequential panels can convey temporal sequence, contrast, and argument. When producing or analyzing comics, consider how panel sequencing is used to make conceptual points or to exemplify theoretical claims.
